Test  weight of response crop grain. Grain test weight is a measurement of grain quality that is calculated by dividing the average weight of a cereal by the volume of a bushel which is 1.244 cubic feet, and is expressed in pounds per bushel. It is a volumetric measurement that accounts for the varying densities of grain that can be caused by weather or production practices.
column4: Grain test weight, often used as a grain quality indicator, is a volumetric measurement based on an official bushel being 1.244 cubic feet. For U.S. No. 1 yellow corn, the official minimum test weight is 56 pounds per bushel. If test weights drop below this standard, the grain price is discounted. Usually, test weights are determined by weighing grain samples filled in a standard dry one-quart measure
